description: Animal skeleton definitions, one per family. The brief allows up to 50 bones per animal skeleton; these stay well under it because the fidelity expectation for animals is medium-to-low and animation coverage matters more than bone count.

shared_rules.rest_pose: standing, legs straight, head level, tail hanging
shared_rules.note: No family shares a skeleton with another. A wolf and a horse differ enough in proportions that sharing would cost more in corrective shapes than it saves in clips.

optional_bones.LeftHorn: antlered and horned species only; dropped for horses and cattle
optional_bones.RightHorn: always dropped or kept with LeftHorn; a one-sided horn is a rigging error
optional_bones.LeftMane: maned species only; dropped for bear and aurochs
optional_bones.RightMane: always dropped or kept with LeftMane
optional_bones.Withers: shoulder-height marker used to seat saddles and loads

optional_bones.RightAntler: always dropped or kept with LeftAntler; a one-sided antler is a rigging error
optional_bones.Muzzle: drives the sniff and graze clips

families.name: animal_skeleton_quadruped_small
families.note: Small mammals are seen at a distance and mostly move as silhouettes; 24 bones is deliberately lean.

notes.flap_glide: Wing1/2/3 drive both flap and glide; glide is a static pose held on Wing1, so no extra bones are needed.
notes.crest: Used for raven, jay, owl and pheasant silhouettes.
notes.perched_vs_flying: One skeleton serves both. Perched clips fold the legs; flying clips tuck them.

families.name: animal_skeleton_fish
families.note: A single spine chain drives swim and turn. Eels use the same skeleton with a longer Body chain, which is why the count is generous for a fish.

notes.why_a_separate_family: Frogs and salamanders cannot use the small-mammal skeleton: a frog's hind limbs fold in two planes for the crouch and the jump, and a salamander's body is a long lateral chain. Sharing would need corrective shapes worth more than the clips it saved.
notes.tail: Salamanders keep Tail1/Tail2; frogs and toads drop them. Dropping a bone never renames the others.
notes.hop_clip: The jump is the defining animation for this family and is the one clip that must not be approximated.

optional_bones.Tail1: salamanders only; frogs and toads drop the tail chain

notes.why_not_the_bird_skeleton: A bat's wing is a membrane stretched across four elongated fingers, not a feathered arm. The bird family's Beak, Crest and tail-feather bones would all be dead weight, and its three-segment wing cannot express the finger-fan that makes a bat silhouette read at night.
notes.size: 14 bones: this is night ambience seen as a fluttering silhouette, not a creature the player studies.
notes.clip: One looping flap plus a glide pose is the whole animation budget for this species.

families.name: animal_skeleton_serpent

optional_bones.LeftLeg: lizard only; dropped for snakes and the slow worm
optional_bones.RightLeg: always dropped or kept with LeftLeg; a one-legged serpent is a rigging error

families.note: Legs are optional: present for the lizard, dropped for the snakes and the slow worm. Dropping a bone must never rename the others.
